prompt: Name a planet, dwarf planet or moon in our Solar System

answers.name: Earth
answers.fact: The only place known to host life.

answers.name: Mars
answers.fact: Olympus Mons is about two and a half times the height of Everest.

answers.name: Jupiter
answers.fact: The Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth.

answers.name: Saturn
answers.fact: Less dense than water: in a big enough bath, it would float.

answers.name: Venus
answers.fact: A day on Venus is longer than its year.

answers.name: Mercury
answers.fact: The smallest planet, but not the hottest. That's Venus.

answers.name: The Moon
answers.fact: Drifts about 3.8 cm further from Earth every year.

answers.name: Pluto
answers.fact: Reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

answers.name: Neptune
answers.fact: Found by maths before anyone saw it, in 1846.

answers.name: Uranus
answers.fact: Spins on its side, tilted about 98 degrees.

answers.name: Titan
answers.fact: The only moon with a thick atmosphere, plus lakes of liquid methane.

answers.name: Europa
answers.fact: Hides a salty ocean under its icy shell.

answers.name: Io
answers.fact: The most volcanically active body in the Solar System.

answers.name: Ganymede
answers.fact: The largest moon in the Solar System: bigger than Mercury.

answers.name: Callisto
answers.fact: One of the most heavily cratered bodies known.

answers.name: Phobos
answers.fact: Spiralling closer to Mars, and will eventually break apart.

answers.name: Deimos
answers.fact: Mars's smaller moon; the name means 'dread'.

answers.name: Charon
answers.fact: So big next to Pluto that the two orbit a point between them.

answers.name: Eris
answers.fact: Its discovery in 2005 helped get Pluto demoted.

answers.name: Triton
answers.fact: Orbits backwards: probably a captured dwarf planet.

answers.name: Enceladus
answers.fact: Fires geysers of water ice into space.

answers.name: Makemake
answers.fact: Named after the creator god of Rapa Nui.

answers.name: Haumea
answers.fact: Spins so fast it's stretched into an egg shape.

answers.name: Mimas
answers.fact: Its giant crater makes it look like the Death Star.

answers.name: Rhea
answers.fact: Saturn's second-largest moon.

answers.name: Iapetus
answers.fact: One side is coal-dark, the other bright as snow.

answers.name: Dione
answers.fact: An icy moon of Saturn streaked with bright cliffs.

answers.name: Tethys
answers.fact: Has a crater, Odysseus, about 400 km wide.

answers.name: Hyperion
answers.fact: Looks like a sponge and tumbles chaotically.

answers.name: Phoebe
answers.fact: Orbits Saturn backwards, likely a captured object.

answers.name: Miranda
answers.fact: Has Verona Rupes, possibly the tallest cliff in the Solar System.

answers.name: Ariel
answers.fact: Uranus's moons are named after Shakespeare and Alexander Pope characters.

answers.name: Umbriel
answers.fact: The darkest of Uranus's big moons.

answers.name: Titania
answers.fact: Uranus's largest moon, named after Shakespeare's fairy queen.

answers.name: Oberon
answers.fact: Named after Titania's husband, the fairy king.

answers.name: Puck
answers.fact: Named after the mischievous sprite from A Midsummer Night's Dream.

answers.name: Nereid
answers.fact: Has one of the most stretched-out orbits of any moon.

answers.name: Proteus
answers.fact: Neptune's second-largest moon.

answers.name: Amalthea
answers.fact: One of the reddest objects in the Solar System.

answers.name: Nix
answers.fact: One of Pluto's small moons, named after the goddess of night.

answers.name: Hydra
answers.fact: Pluto's outermost known moon.

answers.name: Sedna
answers.fact: Takes around 11,000 years to orbit the Sun.

answers.name: Quaoar
answers.fact: Has a ring further out than scientists thought possible.

answers.name: Pandora
answers.fact: A 'shepherd moon' that helps keep Saturn's F ring in shape.

answers.name: Prometheus
answers.fact: Another shepherd of Saturn's F ring.

answers.name: Janus
answers.fact: Swaps orbits with Epimetheus every four years.

answers.name: Epimetheus
answers.fact: Janus's orbit-swapping partner.

answers.name: Pan
answers.fact: Shaped like a ravioli, orbiting inside Saturn's rings.

answers.name: Himalia
answers.fact: The largest of Jupiter's irregular outer moons.

answers.name: Kerberos
answers.fact: One of Pluto's tiny moons, named after the three-headed dog.

answers.name: Styx
answers.fact: Pluto's smallest known moon.

answers.name: Dysnomia
answers.fact: Eris's moon, named after the goddess of lawlessness.

answers.name: Hiʻiaka
answers.fact: Haumea's biggest moon, named after a Hawaiian goddess.

answers.name: Thebe
answers.fact: A small inner moon of Jupiter.

answers.name: Gonggong
answers.fact: A distant dwarf planet candidate named after a Chinese water god.

answers.name: Ceres
answers.fact: The biggest object in the asteroid belt, and the first asteroid ever found, in 1801.
